notes: The universe remains degenerate in the ways integration round 2 recorded and W23 closes none of them: the binding constraint on what a universe knows is still the ruleset rather than the economy, referenceNodesKnown is unmoved at 67.3 to 67.5 (0.01 SE), and these three gate sweeps remain 100 percent passive-control and submit no god verb. What W23 changes is where knowledge LIVES, not how much of it there is.

The two shorter gates are byte-identical on this change and neither could ever have caught the defect it fixes: both cap at worldTickCap 60, four hundred ticks before the library even peaks, and at tick 60 supply still exceeds demand for every occupation. This is the only committed gate with a horizon long enough to see the written record exist at all -- which is itself a finding about the gates, not a reassurance about the change.

Two untuned magnitudes are deliberately left for 0.5.0. The laborer coverage term is blind to laborAffinity by design, so it over-staffs an orcish universe by half and under-staffs a draconic one; and because the obligation it covers includes library upkeep, brake 4 now binds against carrying capacity rather than against a fixed production floor, which makes hoarding cheaper for a universe near K than it was. Both are magnitude questions, and the second is a deliberate trade: a written record that cannot persist makes vision section 5 meaningless.
rationale: W23 populace-and-record: scribe demand, the laborer materials-coverage term, and durability-priced library degradation. Regenerated ONCE, at the end of the workstream. Books now persist -- vision 5's written record went from 0 library instances at tick 2400 to a live, non-monotone shelf -- so referenceGrimoires 220.4 to 785.1 (5.81 SE) and referenceLibraryDepth 9.94 to 31.56 (6.64 SE) are the claimed effect, not drift. They are also the direct inverse of the W7 x W6 interaction the previous regeneration recorded: that note observed depth FALLING 24.94 to 9.94 over the longer horizon because W7's upkeep kept destroying shelves the economy could not pay for, and this change is the reason it can now pay. referencePopulation 19621 to 31331 (5.04 SE) with referencePeakPopulation flat at 50080 to 50310 (1.75 SE) is the same cause and not a second one: K did not move, but the populace is now asked for the laborers its own subsistence and library upkeep require, so the universe sustains a population closer to a carrying capacity that is unchanged. This file is a measurement, not a balance claim: release-plan.md forbids a balance claim before 0.5.0, and every magnitude W23 touched carries tuningStatus untuned.
